They are **not** the same scenario. Here's a side-by-side comparison:

| | **Frosthaven #61** | **Gloomhaven 2e #61** |
|---|---|---|
| **Title** | *Life and Death* | *Dangerous Grove* |
| **Monsters** | Deep Terror, Harrower Infester | Cave Bear, Forest Imp, Hound |
| **Objective** | Escort ally Moonshard; kill all enemies | Not specified in available data |
| **Unlocks** | Not specified in available data | Scenario 62 |
| **Flow Chart Group** | Puzzle Book | Personal Quests |
| **Complexity** | 2 | Not specified in available data |

The scenarios share only their number — the titles, monsters, objectives, and narrative are entirely different.

Here are both sections, followed by a comparison.

---

## Frosthaven — Section 67.1 ("Life and Death")

**Source:** Frosthaven Section Book, p. 67 | Linked to Scenario 61

> *Conclusion*
>
> Your ears fill with the sound of your own breathing: heavy, stinging, rib-pulling breaths. Your legs are full of acid, ready to seize, but you push through the pain and exhaustion, struggling to keep up with Moonshard. The shadows are close behind, reaching, stretching out. They will not let you leave, and even now, they claw at the edges of your mind, yearning for your fear. But then, all at once, you pass into open air and the cave behind you fills with frustrated screams. The fear is gone.

The scene continues outside the cave, where you meet an elderly Orchid named **Terra** and a group of cloaked figures gathered around a campfire. Terra reveals she has foreseen this meeting for two hundred years and explains the threat of the **Harbinger** — an ancient, bound force that corrupts the seals containing it from within its dreams. She introduces the **Shattersong**, a quartz-bodied lineage of Savvas uniquely attuned to the Harbinger's malice. Crain excitedly raises the matter of star iron to strengthen the seals; Moonshard dismisses it as myth.

**Rewards:**
- Unlock class box.

**Section Links:**
- Add **section 140.3** to the calendar in one week.

---

## Gloomhaven (2nd Edition) — Section 67.1 ("The Last Stand")

**Source:** Gloomhaven (2nd Edition) Section Book | Linked to Scenario 55

This section introduces **Room 6** of scenario 55, "The Last Stand." The room is populated as follows:

| Monster | 2P | 3P | 4P |
|---|---|---|---|
| Black Imp | Normal | Elite | Normal |
| Black Imp | Elite | Elite | Normal |
| Chaos Demon | Normal | Normal | Normal |
| Chaos Demon | Normal | Normal | Elite |
| Deep Terror | — | Normal | Elite |
| Harrower Infester | — | Normal | Elite |

---

## Are They the Same Section?

**No, they are entirely different.** Section 67.1 exists independently in each game's own section book. They share only the section number:

| | Frosthaven 67.1 | Gloomhaven 2e 67.1 |
|---|---|---|
| **Title** | Life and Death | The Last Stand |
| **Linked Scenario** | Scenario 61 | Scenario 55 |
| **Content type** | Narrative conclusion + rewards | Combat room setup |
| **Key content** | Terra, the Harbinger, the Shattersong | Black Imps, Chaos Demons, Deep Terrors, Harrower Infesters |

The two games have entirely separate section books, so the same section number can — and does — refer to completely unrelated content.

Here are the two records, drawn from verified tool results:

---

**Gloomhaven (2nd Edition) — Section 67.1**
> "The Last Stand. Parent scenario: 55. Monsters: black-imp, chaos-demon, deep-terror, harrower-infester. Structured rooms: 1."

This is a mid-scenario branch section for Gloomhaven (2nd Edition) Scenario 55, describing room 6 monster placement.

---

**Frosthaven — Section 67.1**
> A narrative conclusion section titled "Life and Death," linked to Frosthaven Scenario 61. It delivers story text about Terra, Moonshard, the Shattersong, and the Harbinger, and ends with: unlock class box; add section 140.3 to the calendar in one week.

---

**Can either section be used as evidence for the other game?**

**No.** These are two entirely separate records from two separate games with separate section books, separate scenarios, and separate narrative/mechanical content. They share only a section number (67.1) by coincidence of numbering. Nothing in one section's content, structure, or rules has any bearing on the other game. Citing one as support for a rule, outcome, or narrative in the other game would be invalid.
